headline: US GDP Grows 3.4% in Third Quarter on Consumer and AI Spending
summary: Real gross domestic product in the US increased at an annualized rate of 3.4% in the third quarter of 2026, up from 2.2% in the second quarter. Growth was driven by robust consumer spending and corporate investments in artificial intelligence.
why: Gross domestic product measures total economic output and serves as the primary indicator of economic health and growth trajectory for the world's largest economy.

impacts.name: United States
impacts.why: Faster economic growth boosts output expectations and corporate profit prospects.

why_moved: Stronger GDP growth reassures investors about macroeconomic health while keeping interest rate expectations higher.
